items.title: The Third and Fourth Ways: Joint Cultivation, and Insight Fueling Concentration Through Joy

items.zh: 第三行者，名為俱得。奢摩他、毘鉢舍那雙雜轉故。第四行者，先已證得初靜慮等，未聽正法，未習多聞；後從大師或餘尊所，聞見諦法，或復得聞斷餘結法；由此得入真諦現觀，或復證得阿羅漢果。
items.en: The third practitioner is called "one who attains both together" — calm and insight turning jointly and interwoven. The fourth practitioner has already attained the first dhyāna and the rest, but has not yet heard the true teaching or undertaken extensive learning. Later, from the Teacher or some other venerable one, he hears the teaching that reveals the truths, or hears the teaching on severing the remaining fetters; by this he enters direct realisation of the truths, or even attains the fruit of arhatship.

items.zh: 彼既證得出離所引大善喜悅，由能制伏諸掉舉心，復還宴坐。如是坐已，安心住於靜慮、等至。
items.en: Having attained the great, wholesome joy drawn forth by release, and being thereby able to subdue every agitated thought, he again sits in stillness; sitting thus, he settles his mind, abiding in the dhyānas and the attainments.

items.title: Summarising the Four Ways by What They Draw Forth

items.zh: 最初趣道，引見道故；第二、第三，引修道故；第四趣道，為俱引故。
items.en: The first way of approach draws forth the path of seeing; the second and third draw forth the path of cultivation; the fourth way of approach draws forth both together.

items.title: The Four Kinds of Purity-Excellence: What "Precepts" Actually Means When Fully Kept

items.zh: 復次，如經中說有四淨勝。為求清淨，此最為勝，故名淨勝。云何為淨？云何為勝？謂所得、所證、所引戒等，若圓滿、若攝受，是名為淨。發勤精進，未滿令滿，是名為勝。
items.en: Furthermore, as the sūtra speaks of four excellences of purity: seeking purity, these are its most excellent forms, hence "excellences of purity." What is "purity"? What is "excellence"? The precepts and the rest that one has obtained, realised, and drawn forth — whether fully completed or become one's very possession — this is called "purity." Rousing diligent effort to complete what is not yet complete is called "excellence."

items.zh: 云何尸羅圓滿攝受？謂若有一，雖住具戒，亦能守護別解脫律儀，而於軌則及所行中未能具足，未於小罪深見怖畏。此於尸羅，未名圓滿。若於一切皆悉滿足，乃名圓滿。如是名為尸羅圓滿。
items.en: What is the fullness and possession of precepts? Someone may abide in complete precepts, and even guard the individual-liberation moral code, yet not be complete in proper conduct and behaviour, and not see with deep dread even minor faults — such a one's precepts are not yet called full. Only when one is complete in every respect is it called "full." This is what is meant by the fullness of precepts.

items.title: Precepts as Second Nature, and the Fullness of Concentration

items.zh: 若於長時串修習故，便於根門善守而住，廣說乃至即於尸羅攝成自體，自性安住。如是名為尸羅攝受。
items.en: If, through long habituation and practice, one comes to guard the sense-doors well and abide so — and so on at length, up to the precepts becoming one's very substance, in which one abides by one's own nature — this is called the possession of precepts.

items.zh: 云何三摩地圓滿？謂若已得加行究竟果，或第四靜慮，乃名圓滿。於此下位，皆未圓滿。云何三摩地攝受？謂彼所得三摩地等後時清淨。又三摩地不為有行之所拘執，乃至廣說。
items.en: What is the fullness of concentration? Only when one has attained the fruit of the consummation of means, or the fourth dhyāna, is it called full; below this level, none of it is yet full. What is the possession of concentration? The concentration one has attained becoming, afterwards, purified — and, moreover, the concentration no longer being gripped by deliberate effort, and so on at length.
What is the completion of view?

items.title: View and Liberation: Purity Completed Only at the Uncontaminated Threshold

items.zh: 謂聞他音，及如理作意故，正見得生。由此正見，雖能知苦乃至知道，若未如實，猶不得名正見圓滿。若能於彼如實了知，爾時方名正見圓滿。云何見攝受？謂於後時諸漏永盡，乃至廣說。
items.en: Right view arises through hearing the teaching from another and through sound attention. By this right view, though one is able to know suffering, up through knowing the path, if this is not yet a true, direct realisation, it is not yet called the fullness of right view. Only when one truly and directly knows these is it called the fullness of right view. What is the possession of view? That afterwards all the outflows are permanently exhausted, and so on at length.

items.zh: 云何解脫圓滿？謂若由有學智見解脫貪等，未名圓滿。若由無學智見得解脫者，乃名圓滿。云何解脫攝受？謂若行、若住，常不退失現法樂住，如是名為解脫攝受。
items.en: What is the fullness of liberation? If release from craving and the rest comes through a trainee's knowledge and vision, it is not yet called full. Only when release comes through an adept's [uncontaminated] knowledge and vision is it called full. What is the possession of liberation? Whether walking or standing still, never losing the pleasant abiding in this very life — this is called the possession of liberation.

items.title: The Mind-Purifying Monk's Five Reflections: Naming the Eight Distracting Thoughts

items.zh: 復次，如經言：心清淨行苾芻，於時時間，應正作意思惟五相，乃至廣說。方便勤修增上心者，乃得名為心清淨行。諸惡不善欲等尋思，及親里等所有尋思，皆於此行能為障礙。略有三種補特伽羅。由軟中上尋思行者，有差別故。
items.en: Furthermore, as the sūtra says: a monk of purifying mind should, from time to time, rightly attend to and contemplate five marks, and so on at length. One who diligently applies himself to cultivating heightened mind is called "one of purifying mind conduct." The various evil, unwholesome discursive thoughts of desire and the rest, and the discursive thoughts of kinsfolk and so on, are all obstacles to this practice. There are, in brief, three kinds of persons, distinguished by whether their discursive thought is soft, middling, or coarse.

items.title: Five Ways to Dislodge a Distracting Thought, Matched to Three Grades of Practitioner

items.zh: 初由正思惟所餘相故，令彼尋思不復現行。第二由見尋思深過患故，或復不念不思惟故，令彼尋思不復現行。云何不念及不思惟？由善於內安心等故。
items.en: The first is that, by rightly attending to some other object, the discursive thought no longer manifests. The second is that, by seeing the deep dangers of the discursive thought, or else by neither dwelling on nor attending to it, the thought no longer manifests. What is "neither dwelling on nor attending to it"? Through skilfully settling the mind inward, and so on.

items.zh: 第三補特伽羅，非初即能令彼一切皆不現行，要當方便令尋思行漸漸歇薄；麁既息已，漸當制伏。若猶未能於尋思路尋思所緣深生厭怖，當以厭患俱行之心多思惟力，於彼尋思俱行之心調練制伏。如是三種補特伽羅，分為五種。
items.en: The third person is not able, from the outset, to make all such thoughts cease manifesting entirely; one must, by skilful means, let the discursive activity gradually thin and weaken — once its coarseness has subsided, one gradually subdues it further. If one still cannot give rise to deep dread towards the path and object of that discursive thought, one should, with a mind conjoined with weariness, apply the power of repeated reflection to train and subdue the mind conjoined with that discursive thought. Thus the three kinds of persons resolve into five methods.

items.title: Refining the Mind Like Gold: Three Stages from Raw Ore to Finished Ornament

items.zh: 復次，盪塵經中，佛世尊言：當如陶鍊生金之法，陶鍊其心，乃至廣說。如是等義云何應知？謂陶鍊生金、略有三種。一、除垢陶鍊，二、攝受陶鍊，三、調柔陶鍊。除垢陶鍊者，謂從金性中、漸漸除去麁中細垢，乃至惟有淨金沙在。攝受陶鍊者，謂即於彼鄭重銷煮。調柔陶鍊者，謂銷煮已，更細鍊治瑕隙等穢。
items.en: Furthermore, in the Sūtra on Washing Away Dust, the World-Honoured Buddha said: "One should refine the mind just as raw gold is refined," and so on at length. How should such matters be understood? The refining of raw gold is, in brief, of three kinds: refining that removes impurities, refining that consolidates, and refining that softens. Refining that removes impurities is gradually removing the coarse, middling, and fine impurities from the gold-bearing ore, until only pure gold-sand remains. Refining that consolidates is earnestly smelting that sand. Refining that softens is, once smelted, further finely working it to remove every flaw and blemish.

items.zh: 如金性內所有生金，種性位中心淨行者，當知亦爾。謂堪能證般涅槃者。問：從何位名心淨行者？答：從得淨信求出家位。此於在家及出家位，有麁、中、細三種垢穢。其在家者由二為障、不令出家。一、不善業。謂常樂安處身語惡行。二、邪惡見。謂撥無世間真阿羅漢正行正至。此於已得淨信位前，能為障礙。
items.en: Just as raw gold exists within gold-bearing ore, so too the mind-purifying practitioner, still at the stage of lineage — the noble path's lineage within the storehouse consciousness — one capable of realising final nirvāṇa — should be understood likewise. Question: from what stage is one called a mind-purifying practitioner? Answer: from the stage of gaining pure faith and seeking to go forth. In both the householder's stage and the renunciant's stage there are coarse, middling, and fine impurities. The householder is obstructed from going forth by two things: unwholesome karma — habitually delighting in unwholesome bodily and verbal conduct; and false view — denying that genuine arhats of right conduct and right attainment truly exist in the world. These obstruct one only before the stage of gaining pure faith.

blocks.text: Today's reading contains two passages meditators have used for centuries: five methods for dislodging distracting thoughts (from the *Vitakkasaṇṭhāna Sutta*), and the simile of refining gold. Both are about patience with the mind.
The third and fourth ways of approaching the path are joint cultivation and insight fuelling concentration through joy.

Four "purities and excellences": of **precepts**, **concentration**, **view**, and **liberation**. What one has obtained is "purity"; rousing effort to complete it is "excellence". Master Cháng Bǎi on precepts: keeping the root precepts while being careless about deportment in walking, standing, sitting, and lying is not full purity. Possession of precepts is when they "become one's very substance". Venerable Miào Jìng: "his body, speech, and mind have become one with the precepts." Fullness of view, Master Cháng Bǎi says, requires non-discriminating wisdom. Fullness of liberation comes only with an adept's knowledge; a trainee's release is not yet full.

One "who diligently cultivates heightened mind" is called a monk of purifying-mind conduct. Eight kinds of distracting thought obstruct him. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Compendium of Topics*: thoughts of desire, ill will, harm, kinsfolk, homeland, not-dying, contempt for others, and family influence. (Compare Day 78.)

subs.head: Five ways to dislodge a thought

items: **Attend to another object**, so the thought stops. Master Cháng Bǎi: "like a skilled carpenter driving out a coarse peg with a fine one".
**Do not attend to it**: neither think of it nor engage it.
**Let its activity gradually thin**, tracing it back to its cause.
**Suppress it by force**. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the meditation master Pa-Auk Sayadaw: "clench the teeth, press the tongue to the palate, and with the mind crush the evil thought".

blocks.text: The treatise matches these to three grades of practitioner. Venerable Miào Jìng reads the grading differently from the *Pīxún jì*: he takes the first as the method of the strongest practitioner and the last as the method of the weakest. Gentle methods first; force only when nothing else works.

Gold ore is refined in three stages: removing impurities, consolidating, and softening, until the smith can shape it into any ornament. So with the mind. Master Cháng Bǎi maps the stages: from the first aspiration to the first dhyāna is removing impurities; the second to fourth dhyānas, consolidating; mastery of the supernormal knowledges, softening. Only refined gold can be made into an ornament; only a refined mind can be shaped at will.
Some cannot even begin: a householder held back by "unwholesome karma" or "false view, denying that genuine arhats exist". The first refinement is simply turning towards the path.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are "purity" and "excellence"?
options: the precepts and the rest obtained, realised, drawn forth, whether complete or possessed — purity; rousing effort to complete what isn't complete — excellence
quiz.why: "The precepts and the rest that one has obtained, realised, and drawn forth — whether fully completed or become one's very possession — this is called purity. Rousing diligent effort to complete what is not yet complete is called excellence." Master Cháng Bǎi: the *Saṃyukta* names purity of precepts, mind, view, liberation.

quiz.q: Possession of precepts is when they "become one's very substance." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe it?
options: merged with the precepts — body, speech, and mind one with them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "It has merged into one with him — his body, speech, and mind have become one with the precepts." Master Cháng Bǎi: a stream-enterer has full precepts but not yet possession.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are fullness and possession of liberation?
options: release through an adept's knowledge is full; never losing present happiness whether walking or standing is possession
quiz.why: "If release from craving and the rest comes through a trainee's knowledge and vision, it is not yet called full. Only when release comes through an adept's knowledge and vision is it called full … Whether walking or standing still, never losing the pleasant abiding in this very life — this is called the possession of liberation." Venerable Miào Jìng: only at buddhahood is it most complete.

quiz.q: Discursive thoughts of desire and of kinsfolk obstruct this practice. Per Master Cháng Bǎi citing the Compendium of Topics, how many kinds?
options: eight: desire, ill will, harm, kinsfolk, homeland, not-dying, contempt, family influence
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The Compendium of Topics lists eight: thoughts of desire, ill will, harm, kinsfolk, homeland, not-dying," plus contempt and family influence. Venerable Miào Jìng: "contempt" is arrogance; "family influence" is boasting of patrons. The note's "Compendium of Determinations" is wrong (logged).

quiz.q: What is the first method to dislodge a distracting thought, and what simile does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: attending rightly to another object so the thought stops — like a skilled carpenter driving out a coarse peg with a fine one
quiz.why: "The first is that, by rightly attending to some other object, the discursive thought no longer manifests." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing Pa-Auk Sayadaw: "Like a skilled carpenter or apprentice using a fine peg to knock out, remove, and extract a coarse peg."

quiz.q: The text divides three persons by soft, middling, and coarse discursive thought. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say about which is superior?
options: opposite to the Pixunji — he holds the first is superior, the last inferior, graded by the practitioner's strength of calm and insight
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Reading this text, my view is the opposite — I think the first is superior and the last inferior." The grading is by the practitioner's calm and insight. The translation reads it as the thoughts' coarseness.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what three kinds of refining gold are there?
options: refining that removes impurities, that consolidates, and that softens
quiz.why: "Refining that removes impurities, refining that consolidates, and refining that softens." Removing impurities until pure gold-sand remains; smelting it; then finely removing flaws. Venerable Miào Jìng: separate grains fused into one great ingot.
